conclusion: No remaining production correctness blocker found in the reviewed final implementation. Final author typecheck/export checkpoint remains required; no root application or live quality gain is certified.

resolvedFindings.finding: json_each decodes string elements; reparsing a JSON-looking archived string changed role/text and could collide with a distinct active object during ROW_NUMBER deduplication.
resolvedFindings.resolution: The keyword archive SQL projection re-encodes scalar JSON before deduplication and the single parse; objects/arrays and true/false retain their original JSON type. Legacy literal search retains its original projection.

resolvedFindings.finding: The prior SQLite getConversationHistory path could reinterpret archived JSON-looking text or discard active scalar string text after search located it.
resolvedFindings.resolution: The transcript path uses the same scalar-preserving archive projection and the existing in-memory payload decoder, moved verbatim to a shared helper. Session/archive ACL and 4000-character text bounds stay in place.

resolvedFindings.finding: Equal-date duplicate preference differed between SQLite binary ID ordering and in-memory localeCompare for mixed-case/Unicode IDs.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Keyword-only in-memory duplicate tie now uses Buffer.compare on UTF-8 bytes, matching SQLite BINARY ordering. Active-before-archive and newest-before-date-filter behavior is retained.

resolvedFindings.finding: Author regression showed the installed Bun runtime reports a pure numeric Segmenter token as not word-like, so the previous isWordLike gate discarded numeric identifiers.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Admissibility now uses the existing Unicode letter/number predicate without isWordLike. Normalization, stop words, all term/query limits and punctuation-only literal fallback remain. This explicitly affects both memory and conversation keyword retrieval.

assessment.acl: Native search always passes the asserted canonical principal org/user and Super Agent restriction. Both adapters apply tenant, user, profile, importing-profile, Super Agent and date filters before lexical scoring/top-K, so inaccessible rows cannot consume result slots. Database userId remains optional for trusted callers as before; the native boundary does not omit it.
assessment.sqlDedupBeforeAcl: The SQL window over org rows precedes some owner/profile filters, but partitions only within each session and does not assign lexical relevance or a result cap. This is a resource-cost concern, not an identified output ACL bypass.
assessment.ranking: Bounded weighted OR of unique normalized term substrings is a reasonable topic-search contract. More matching terms rank above fewer; fixed capped length weights and deterministic tie ordering apply. It is not phrase matching, stemming, semantic retrieval or a guarantee of useful natural-language recall.
assessment.topK: The collector retains at most K matches (DB maximum200; native tool maximum50) and searches all eligible history before limiting. This avoids truncating older strong matches behind newer weak matches.
assessment.totalWork: Total work is not bounded by K. SQLite may sort/materialize all org rows for its window. In-memory scans all archives for every eligible session, materializes per-session candidates/serialized seen keys, and sorts candidates. Do not advertise bounded total memory, constant latency, or total adapter linear time.
assessment.duplicateContract: Identity is exact serialized payload within a session, with active then newest then binary-ID preference. Deduplication occurs before date filtering, so an older archived copy is intentionally not revived when a newer preferred copy falls outside the date window. This is not semantic duplicate detection.
assessment.archiveParity: Scalar-preserving keyword projection avoids conflating literal JSON strings with objects/numbers/booleans/null. A shared decoder retains original text and excludes message-envelope metadata from lexical search. Legacy-null fallback semantics are retained rather than inventing new text.
assessment.literalCompatibility: Omitting matchMode or explicitly selecting literal retains the prior direct database search path. SQL still uses its historical LIKE pattern behavior and serialized payload matching; in-memory still searches decoded content. This patch does not newly promise cross-adapter literal wildcard/metadata parity. The native search_chats tool intentionally switches to keywords.
assessment.testsContract: Replacing old lexical-query exact-cardinality expectations with positive exact-source target checks and explicit forbidden-session exclusion is appropriate. Existing authorization tests still verify no private-only/super/cross-org access. An importing-session keyword fixture is not claimed because the public SQLite adapter refuses to create such a session; existing profile atomic-import regressions cover reservation publication rules.

recommendations: Complete and preserve final focused TypeScript/lint/behavior gates before exporting or integrating.
Keep current archive/string/object/scalar and reopen regressions, including a JSON-looking archived literal whose metadata-shaped text differs from an actual active object.
Retain direct literal mode tests alongside native keyword behavior; describe native results as lexical topic matches.

If production history size later requires it, design tenant/user/profile-scoped indexed candidate retrieval or query cancellation with explicit recall tradeoffs. The current collector bound alone is not a scalability proof.
Do not claim live recall, learning or comparative harness improvement from these offline source/behavior checks.
